report.title: Checkout slowdown: inventory DB pool contention
report.summary: During the incident window, checkout latency and errors increased while payment and DB CPU stayed near baseline. Slow traces concentrate time in inventory-api waiting to acquire DB connections. A recent release reduced the inventory client pool max, temporally aligned with the slowdown.

findings.text: checkout-api p95 latency rose to 2840ms and error rate to 6.8% while request rate stayed ~120 rps during 14:15–14:30 UTC.
Representative slow trace shows most time in inventory.reserve, dominated by db.pool.acquire wait (2190ms); 18/20 slow samples show pool waits >1800ms.
Payment authorization p95 stayed near baseline (~140ms), while DB CPU stayed near baseline (~36%), but pending pool requests increased from 0 to 84.
A release at 14:12 UTC reduced the inventory client connection pool maximum from 20 to 5; the latency increase starts at 14:15, consistent with a pool contention hypothesis.

nextSteps: Compare inventory-api DB pool acquire wait, pool pending, and concurrency metrics across the pre-14:12 and post-14:12 cohorts to quantify the change in contention.

report.uncertainty: Traces are sampled (18/20 slow samples) and do not represent all requests. The timing of the pool-limit change aligns with the slowdown, but the evidence does not by itself confirm causality or exclude other inventory-path contributors.
report.customerUpdate: Between 14:15–14:30 UTC we observed elevated checkout latency and API errors. Current evidence indicates delays primarily in the inventory reservation step while waiting on database connections; payment processing latency appears normal. We are validating whether a recent configuration change increased connection contention.
